answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall, failing to hold the onyx of valid state. A verifier challenges agents by requesting specific memory indices; failure to return data matching the ember-like flicker of the working set triggers an immediate penalty. Every umber-toned piece of logic must reside on a unique bus to prevent pooling. Honest participants pay 120 watts for status; fakes pay 120,000 watts, rendering mass-identity farms infeasible.
